title: Family Picnic Snacks: Uniform Fruit Tartlets Made with a Scoop
keyword: fruit tartlets cookie dough scoop picnic
meta_description: Discover how to make uniform fruit tartlet snack packs for picnics using a cookie dough scoop—quick, tidy, and perfect for on‑the‑go families.
html:
When you’re planning a family picnic, the easiest way to keep kids (and adults) happy is with bite‑size fruit tartlets that are both beautiful and portable. The secret to getting each tartlet the same size and shape? A cookie dough scoop. This tool lets you drop consistent portions of dough, fruit filling, and glaze, so every bite looks as good as it tastes.

Why uniform fruit tartlets matter for picnics

Uniformity isn’t just about aesthetics; it’s about practicality. When every tartlet is the same size, you can:

  • Pack them tightly in a container without crushing the tops.
  • Know exactly how many servings you have – no guesswork.
  • Serve a balanced snack: each tartlet holds the same amount of fruit, crust, and glaze, keeping sugar and calories consistent.

Using a cookie dough scoop eliminates the need for a kitchen scale or a lot of guesswork, and it speeds up the prep time dramatically.

Choosing the right scoop for fruit tartlets

The Cookie Dough Scoop comes in a range of sizes, from miniature ½‑inch scoops perfect for mini tartlets up to larger 2‑inch scoops for fuller pastries. For a standard picnic‑friendly tartlet, the 1‑inch scoop hits the sweet spot – it yields a crust about 1½ inches in diameter, which is easy for little hands to hold.

Because the scoop is designed for dough, it also works wonderfully for fruit fillings. The smooth release mechanism means the filling doesn’t cling to the scoop, keeping the tops clean and the edges crisp.

Step‑by‑step recipe: Uniform fruit tartlet snack packs

Here’s a straightforward recipe that showcases the scoop’s versatility. You’ll need the following:

  1. 1 cup all‑purpose flour
  2. ¼ cup unsalted butter, cold and cubed
  3. ¼ cup powdered sugar
  4. ¼ teaspoon salt
  5. 1 egg yolk
  6. 2‑3 tablespoons cold water (as needed)
  7. 1 cup mixed fresh fruit (berries, diced kiwi, mango)
  8. ¼ cup apricot jam for glaze

Directions:

1. Make the crust dough. In a food processor pulse the flour, butter, powdered sugar, and salt until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Add the egg yolk and just enough cold water to bring the dough together. Form into a ball, wrap in plastic, and chill for 30 minutes.

2. Prepare the fruit filling. Toss the fresh fruit with a pinch of sugar and a splash of lemon juice. Let sit for 10 minutes, then drain any excess liquid.

3. Roll and scoop. On a lightly floured surface, roll the dough to about ¼‑inch thickness. Using the Cookie Dough Scoop (1‑inch size), press the scoop into the dough and lift out a perfect circle. Place each circle onto a parchment‑lined baking sheet.

4. Add filling. With the same scoop, portion the fruit mixture onto the center of each crust circle. Aim for a small mound that will sit nicely under the glaze.

5. Bake. Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Bake the tartlets for 12‑15 minutes, until the edges turn golden brown.

6. Glaze. Warm the apricot jam until fluid, then brush a thin layer over each tartlet while they’re still warm. The glaze gives a glossy finish and helps seal in moisture.

Let the tartlets cool completely before packing them in a reusable container. They stay fresh for up to two days at room temperature, making them ideal for a day‑long outing.

Packing tips for a hassle‑free picnic

Even the best‑made tartlets can get soggy if they sit in a damp environment. Here’s how to keep them crisp:

  • Use parchment paper. Layer a sheet of parchment between each row of tartlets to prevent them from sticking together.
  • Separate the glaze. If you prefer a less shiny finish, you can omit the glaze and drizzle it just before serving.
  • Cool before sealing. Ensure the tartlets are completely cool before placing the lid on the container; trapped steam will soften the crust.

Pair the fruit tartlets with a simple cheese stick or a handful of nuts for a balanced snack that satisfies sweet and savory cravings.

Beyond fruit: Using the scoop for other picnic treats

The Cookie Dough Scoop isn’t limited to fruit tartlets. Its size options let you create a whole family‑style snack station:

  • Mini chocolate chip cookies for a quick dessert.
  • Meatball “pops” seasoned with herbs – perfect for a protein boost.
  • Mini muffin batters for a savory cheese‑and‑herb bite.

Having a single tool that can handle dough, filling, and even meat mixtures means less clutter in your picnic basket and fewer utensils to wash at home.

FAQ

Can I use the scoop with a gluten‑free crust?

Yes. The scoop works with any dough consistency, so simply substitute the all‑purpose flour for a gluten‑free blend and follow the same steps.

How do I prevent the fruit from leaking out during baking?

Make sure the fruit filling isn’t overly wet. After tossing the fruit with sugar and lemon, let it sit briefly, then pat dry with paper towels before scooping.

Is the Cookie Dough Scoop dishwasher safe?

It is. The scoop’s stainless‑steel construction can be placed on the top rack of a dishwasher, or you can wash it by hand with warm, soapy water for extra longevity.
